title: Combine Skills and MCP to Close the Context Gap — Pedro Rodrigues, Supabase
talk_summary: Pedro Rodrigues describes Supabase's product skill for agents: MCP/tools provide capabilities, but product-specific guidance closes the context gap. He shares principles for writing skills and eval results showing MCP+skill beats MCP alone across models.

takeaways.what_they_do: They give agents a product-specific skill alongside MCP tools, so tools supply actions while the skill supplies required guidance and security workflow.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the skills plus the MCP uh outperform any other conditions on every model that we we tested
takeaways.numbers: 6 scenarios, 4 agents from 2 vendors, 3 conditions; MCP+skill outperformed every model

takeaways.what_they_do: They moved a non-negotiable security checklist from a reference file into the main skill because agents skipped reference files.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if something can get skipped it will be skipped

takeaways.what_they_do: The skill prescribes the exact preferred sequence for common product operations, such as direct DDL in dev/staging, run advisor, fix issues, then create migration.
takeaways.evidence_quote: be opinionated. You know your product the best

takeaways.technique: Point to single source of truth
takeaways.what_they_do: The skill avoids duplicating documentation and persistently tells the agent where and how to fetch current docs.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Just point the agent to it to the most up-to-date

takeaways.what_they_do: They test the markdown skill with evals across scenarios, models, and conditions, scoring task completeness.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we can now test um documents. We can now test documentation

takeaways.what_they_do: They package skills in repos/plugins so they are discoverable and distributed with the code.
takeaways.evidence_quote: packaging the skills on the the repos themselves
